stage1.impression: Reads as a CG showroom alcove, not a photographed bar: two speakers wash out to white and grey under hot spots, so no tint reads and the horns look like black glass TV screens. The Orb lamps are flat, blown white discs, and a big featureless salmon block (a chair back) fills the lower centre. The fir lining looks like a clean repeating texture, and no concrete, steel or sign of life is visible. A design magazine would not run this as a specific place; it reads as a generic hi-fi demo room.

blocking_9: The Smoke tint must read on the speaker cabinets at a glance: speaker body region r/g/b not neutral grey, lum_p95 under 235, white batts visible through the acrylic, not as the surface
The foreground chair must read as dark velvet with pile and fall-off, darker than the speakers, and not block the altar's centre
The Orb lamps must glow as smoked acrylic with a frosted liner, not as flat white discs (lum_p95 under 220)
Frame lum_median between 24 and 40, with the shadows holding detail
At least one surface of the shell (board-formed concrete or blackened steel) visible at 1:1 with real texture, and fir boards with per-board variation, checks and end grain instead of a uniform tile
Signs of life in frame (glass, record out of sleeve, coat) and no bright screens cut by the frame edges

defects.what: Left Tropos washes out to neutral grey-white (median 129, r137 g127 b124): no smoked tint, the white batts read as the surface
Right Tropos, same washout, and an identical pose and lighting, so it reads as a copy
Horn reads as a black glossy screen with smeared, wobbly reflections (denoiser smear)
Plinth top hot under the altar spot, clips at 0.32%
Foreground tub chair: a flat salmon block (median 140, r190 g129 b98), brighter than the room and the speakers, with no velvet pile, no shading and visible grain; it blocks the altar
Orb lamp a blown, neutral-white flat disc (median 235), no smoke tint, no liner depth
Second Orb, same blown white disc, cut by the frame edge
Fir lining reads as a uniform repeating board texture: low range (42.6), no checks, nail holes or end grain
Spot beams draw hard CG cones on the fir above each speaker
A bright screen or panel cut by the left frame edge (median 119) pulls the eye out of frame
A bright panel cut by the right frame edge
Altar step and floor fall to murk (median 16.6); the 200 mm step and floor don't read
Ceiling is an empty black band (median 7), no beams or concrete detail
Side table and record player look flat and toy-like; the white napkin or sleeve is the brightest neutral there

changes.problem: The altar spots blow the speakers to neutral white, so the Smoke tint and the depth of the acrylic are lost and the plinths clip.

evidence.measured: lum_median 196.6, lum_p95 250.9, r201 g196 b193 (neutral); plinth top 360,490-470,535 clip 0.32%

change.to: 70 W, 2400 K, cone 22 deg, aimed at cabinet mid-height so the plinth tops fall off

changes.expected: The cabinets drop to a median of about 100 to 140 with the smoked tint visible over the batts; the plinth tops stop clipping.

changes.problem: The foreground tub chair is the brightest large surface in the frame and reads as a flat salmon block, not dark velvet.

evidence.measured: lum_median 139.8, lum_range 100, r190 g129 b98; brighter than the fir (47)

change.setting: the Domes' downlights and the record wall's spots (whatever hits the chair backs), and the velvet's finish
change.from: Domes' downlights 32.0 W; velvet lit flat
change.to: Domes' downlights 18 W, or aim them off the zone; give the velvet a sheen and pile (darker at normal, lighter at the grazing edge) so the back falls off top to bottom

changes.expected: The chair back sits at a median of about 45 to 75, darker than the speakers, with a visible pile highlight along its rim.

changes.problem: The camera sits squarely behind a chair whose back fills the lower centre and blocks the altar, and the 26 mm lens makes the alcove feel like a distant stage.

evidence.measured: The chair covers 6.4% of the frame at the centre-bottom; the speakers fill under 5% each

change.to: position about [12.6, 3.05, 1.05] (seated eye level, between the two tub chairs), lens 35 mm, f/2.8 focused on the nearer speaker, so the chair arms frame the altar from either side

changes.expected: The speakers become the clear hero (about 10% of the frame each), the chairs read as framing silhouettes, and the frame is closer and cozier.

changes.problem: The Orb lamps render as blown, neutral white discs, so their smoked acrylic and frosted liner don't read and they look like CG emitters.

evidence.measured: lum_median 235, r238 g235 b231 (neutral); left Orb 465,560-535,630 median 235

change.to: 0.12 W, glow 0.003, with the frosted liner's roughness raised so the glow is soft and the smoked shell darkens the rim

changes.expected: The Orbs read as warm smoked glows at about 150 to 200, with a darker rim and visible tint, and throw a small pool on the table.

changes.problem: Once the hot spots come down, the frame sits under the target and the floor, step and ceiling fall to murk.

evidence.measured: Frame lum_median 19.9 (target 22 to 50); step 200,520-1000,580 median 16.6; ceiling median 7.1

change.setting: render: exposure, plus a grazing light
change.to: exposure 5.2 after c1 and c2; haze 0.005; a 6 W 2700 K linear strip under the altar step's nosing so the 200 mm step reads

changes.expected: Frame median of about 26 to 36; the step edge reads as a thin warm line; the ceiling holds faint detail.

changes.problem: The Douglas fir lining reads as a uniform tiled texture with no checks, nail holes or tone shifts board to board.

evidence.measured: lum_range 42.6, falloff bins 34 to 56; boards repeat with identical figure

change.from: one tiled board texture, even sheen
change.to: per-board random UV offset and ±12% tone, a darker oiled finish, a soft roughness of 0.55, shallow checks and occasional nail holes, and darker end grain at the niche returns

changes.expected: The wall reads as real old fir under a spot, with each board distinct and its range widening.

changes.problem: The card's props (a record out of its sleeve, a sleeve against a plinth, a coat over a tub chair, glasses) don't read in this frame, so the room looks unused.

evidence.measured: Seen: only a white rectangle on the side table; no glass, coat or record visible

change.from: a coat over a tub chair, a sleeve against a plinth (not legible)
change.to: a dark wool coat over the near chair's arm, a rocks glass with a lit highlight on each side table, a record sleeve leaning on the left plinth's front, facing the camera

changes.expected: Two or three small warm highlights and one soft textile in the foreground: a sign of life.

changes.problem: The bright screens or panels cut by both frame edges pull the eye out of the frame.

evidence.measured: lum_median 119 at the left edge; the right edge 1160-1200 also bright

change.setting: the room's glowing surfaces: the screens' images
change.to: 0.012 (or reframe with c3 so they leave the frame)

changes.expected: The edges sit under about 50, so the eye stays on the altar.

out_of_scope.request: Make the Tropos horns read less like black glass screens (shape and resin)
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's shape and parts are fixed; only the light on it can change (c1).

out_of_scope.request: Show the white batts less through the cabinet
out_of_scope.why: The white batts inside the tinted cabinets are part of the fixed product.

out_of_scope.request: A single speaker as the only colour
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes a pair on the altar.

out_of_scope.request: Board-formed concrete visible in this view
out_of_scope.why: The niche's fir lining is fixed design; concrete can only enter through the camera (c3) if the shell shows at the sides.
